items.title: The TCA intermediates: six versions read AI
items.where: Some Causes of poor gut health, P24
items.your_version: Malic and citric acid (which make green apples and tart cherries sour) are quick energy sources for the lining cells of your small intestines. That's because they are intermediate products in the cells' mitochondrial energy production cycle, called TCA, Krebs, or citric acid cycle. Glutamine also fuels that same cycle via a different route, as it converts to a-KG, while also providing nitrogen to help build new cells. Those lining cells then use the energy they get from those fuels to heal the gut lining by pulling the tight junctions together.

items.my_version: Malic and citric acid are what's called TCA cycle intermediates. TCA is another name for the citric acid cycle, the one the glutamine ends up in, and these acids are already part of it, so your mitochondria can use them for energy directly. They're the acids that make green apples and tart cherries sour, so eating clean sour stuff like that, or taking organic malic acid, gets the cells lining your gut another fuel, and quickly. Glutamine has to be turned into α-KG first, so that's a different biochemical route, but either way those cells then use the extra energy to heal the gut lining faster.
